The fault is in [config/syslogconf.go](/app/config/syslogconf.go:13): `SyslogConf` and `Validate()` live in `config`, and `config/syslog` does not exist. [config/config.go](/app/config/config.go:53) stores that type and calls its validator; [reporter/syslog.go](/app/reporter/syslog.go:18) also depends on its severity and facility methods.

The fix needs a public `config/syslog.Conf` with the specified fields and `Validate()`, while preserving enabled-only validation and one error per invalid protocol, port, severity, or facility. Windows needs the specified enabled-only rejection. Existing Linux tests pass (`TestSyslogConfValidate`); dedicated-package and Windows behavior are not covered by those tests.

I recorded the diagnosis in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). Project source and tests were not edited because this assignment restricts my role to fault localization.

Moved syslog configuration into the public [config/syslog package](/app/config/syslog/types.go), with a `Conf.Validate()` method and Windows-specific rejection when syslog is enabled. Config and reporter now use the new type; `config.SyslogConf` remains an alias for existing callers.

The existing and new tests pass with `go test ./config/syslog ./config ./reporter`. The Windows config and syslog test binaries also cross-compile.

VERDICT: FIX

The patch exposes `config/syslog.Conf` and its validation methods, and the relevant Linux tests pass. One test suite issue remains: [config/config_test.go](/app/config/config_test.go:9) runs on Windows and expects up to four field errors, but the required Windows validator returns exactly one error whenever syslog is enabled. Make those test expectations platform specific.

- `GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./config/syslog ./config ./reporter` — passed, all three packages.
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test -c -o .codex-role-output/syslog_windows.test.exe ./config/syslog` — passed compilation.
